column1: # Secure Linux app equivalents. Tab-separated; do not use tabs inside a field.
# pattern: case-insensitive substring of the old app name. More specific patterns come first.
# linux_id / pkg_type: the only Fedora package that an "extra" row may install (flatpak or rpm).
# debian_pkg: Debian package for the same linux_id; BLANK means unavailable on Debian (never guess).
# state: installed = already included or handled by a built-in; extra = optional recommendation; gap = no good open equivalent.
# profiles: all, full or lite. An installed app outside the current profile is reported honestly, not called covered.

column7: It covers almost everything home and school documents need; complex macros and exact layout can differ.

column5: LibreOffice Calc replaces Apple Numbers for spreadsheets.

column5: LibreOffice Impress replaces Apple Keynote for presentations.

column5: Joplin replaces Evernote with notebooks, tags, search and attachments.
column6: It is open, imports Evernote exports and does not require a notes subscription.
column7: Most notes import well; some proprietary notebook and collaboration features do not.

column5: Joplin replaces Apple Notes with searchable notebooks on this computer.
column6: It is open, works offline and keeps your notes in a portable format.
column7: Apple Notes must be exported first; handwriting and iCloud sharing do not carry across exactly.

column5: Scribus lays out newsletters, flyers and booklets, replacing Microsoft Publisher.
column6: It is the strongest open desktop-publishing app, with precise text, colour and print controls.
column7: It is powerful but less template-led; Publisher files usually need rebuilding or PDF import.

column5: ProjectLibre plans tasks, dates and dependencies, replacing Microsoft Project.
column6: It is the closest open project planner and can read many Microsoft Project files.
column7: It covers ordinary plans; enterprise Project Server and complex files are not fully compatible.

column5: draw.io makes flowcharts, network maps and diagrams, replacing Visio.
column6: It is much easier for ordinary diagrams, works offline and saves in an open, portable format.
column7: It covers most diagrams; specialised Visio stencils and data-linked diagrams may not transfer.

column5: Xero still works in the web browser, so there is nothing new to install.
column6: Using the real service keeps payroll, invoices and accountant access exactly the same.
column7: This is the official Xero web app, not an open replacement; bookmarks and passwords can come across.

column5: GnuCash tracks accounts, income and spending, replacing basic QuickBooks bookkeeping.
column6: It is mature, private and double-entry, with no company holding your financial file.
column7: There is no perfect equivalent: payroll, bank feeds, Australian tax and accountant workflows may be missing.

column5: GnuCash replaces basic MYOB bookkeeping with private accounts and reports.
column6: It is the best-established open accounting app for home and small-business books.
column7: It is not a like-for-like MYOB replacement: payroll, tax, bank feeds and accountant exchange can be missing.

column5: PDF Arranger merges, splits, reorders and rotates PDFs, replacing common Acrobat Pro jobs.
column6: It does the everyday page work simply, while LibreOffice Draw can edit some PDF text and graphics.
column7: Advanced forms, reliable redaction, signatures and OCR are not a complete Acrobat Pro replacement.

column5: The built-in document viewer opens, searches and prints PDFs, replacing Adobe Reader.
column6: It is already part of the desktop, starts quickly and needs no Adobe account.
column7: It covers normal reading and forms; uncommon PDF features can differ.

column5: The built-in image and document viewers replace Preview for looking at pictures and PDFs.
column6: They are already part of the desktop and open files without an account.
column7: Basic viewing and printing are covered; every Apple annotation trick is not identical.

column5: LibreWolf replaces Chrome with a private browser based on Firefox.
column6: It removes tracking, blocks many trackers and can import Chrome bookmarks and passwords.

column5: LibreWolf replaces Edge with a private browser based on Firefox.
column6: It has strong tracking protection and can import Edge bookmarks and passwords.
column7: Websites and ordinary extensions work well; Microsoft-specific syncing and features do not.

column5: LibreWolf replaces Safari with a private browser based on Firefox.
column6: It is independent, open and protects against trackers by default.
column7: Bookmarks can be imported; Apple Pay, iCloud tabs and Safari extensions do not transfer.

column5: LibreWolf is Firefox with stronger privacy settings already switched on.
column6: It keeps Firefox compatibility while removing Mozilla tracking and sponsored content.
column7: Most Firefox extensions work; Firefox account sync needs separate consideration.

column5: There is no open replacement for a retired Skype account and its contacts.
column6: The honest option is to choose a current call service with the people you contact.
column7: Microsoft retired Skype in 2025; another open app cannot recreate the old service.

column5: There is no fully open Zoom-compatible app that reliably joins every Zoom meeting.
column6: Use Zoom's official web app when a meeting requires Zoom; Jami is open but calls Jami users instead.
column7: An open replacement cannot promise Zoom meeting compatibility or the same host features.

column5: There is no fully open Teams-compatible app with complete meeting and work-account support.
column6: The official Teams web app is the reliable choice for Teams links and work sign-in.
column7: Open chat apps cannot replace an organisation's Teams service or guarantee every meeting feature.

column5: There is no good open equivalent that joins FaceTime calls.
column6: Ask the caller for a browser-based meeting link, or use an open service such as Jami with them.
column7: FaceTime is Apple-only; another app cannot connect to its closed calling network.

column5: There is no dependable open WhatsApp desktop client with the same account and calls.
column6: The official WhatsApp web app is the safe compatible choice; Signal is open but uses a different network.
column7: Unofficial clients can break or risk the account, and WhatsApp's service is not open.

column5: There is no dependable open Messenger desktop client with the same account and features.
column6: Use the official Messenger web app, or choose an open messenger with your contacts.
column7: Facebook's network is closed; open alternatives cannot recreate its contact list or calls.

column5: Telegram Desktop signs in to the same Telegram chats and calls.
column6: It is the official open-source desktop client, so compatibility is better than with unofficial copies.
column7: Chats come from the same Telegram service; ordinary cloud chats are not end-to-end encrypted.

column5: Vesktop is an open desktop client for the same Discord servers and messages.

column7: It still uses Discord's non-open service; unofficial client changes can break when Discord changes.

column5: There is no fully open Slack-compatible client with complete support.
column6: Use Slack's official web app for work; open chat systems cannot reproduce a workplace Slack account.
column7: The service and some desktop features are proprietary.

column5: There is no complete open replacement for Spotify's catalogue and account.
column6: Spotify's web player is the compatible choice; open clients still need Spotify and often a paid account.
column7: An open music player cannot supply the same licensed catalogue or recommendations.

column5: Steam is already installed for your Steam library and account.
column6: The full setup includes the real client plus tools that help Windows games run on Linux.
column7: Many games work through Proton, but some anti-cheat games do not.

column5: Heroic opens Epic Games and GOG libraries without their heavy launchers.

column7: Most games work; store social features, anti-cheat and individual Windows games can fail.

column5: Heroic opens GOG and Epic Games libraries in one open launcher.
column6: It is private, lightweight and supports GOG's offline installers and real account.
column7: Most games work; Windows-only games and anti-cheat can still be a problem.

column5: Kdenlive edits video with effects and titles, replacing ordinary After Effects work.

column7: Plain text is easy; rich Apple documents may need exporting first.

column7: Apple loops, instruments and GarageBand projects do not transfer; recording bands is better in Ardour.

column5: Audacity is already installed for recording and editing sound.

column7: It is not the same hosted drive: Google sharing, Docs and web-only files are not reproduced.

column5: Syncthing replaces Dropbox for synchronising folders between your own devices.
column6: It is open, private and has no storage quota from a cloud company.
column7: It does not provide Dropbox web sharing or hosted backups; devices need to be online to sync.

column5: The built-in archive tool opens and makes zip, 7z and rar files, replacing WinRAR.
column6: It is already integrated with the file manager and needs no licence reminder.
column7: Common archives work; rare recovery and encryption options can differ.

column5: The built-in archive tool opens and makes compressed files, replacing 7-Zip.
column6: It works from the file manager and supports the formats most people receive.
column7: Every advanced 7-Zip switch is not exposed, but ordinary archives are covered.

column6: It is the most trusted open torrent client, with search, limits and a clean interface.
column7: Torrents and magnet links work; the interface and any uTorrent-only features differ.

column6: The system's permissions, signed packages and updates stop most threats without a security subscription.
column7: This is a different approach, not an identical Norton suite; scan files before passing them to Windows PCs.

column5: Linux does not need McAfee's always-on antivirus; ClamAV is provided for on-demand file scans.
column6: Signed updates and ordinary user permissions provide the main protection without adverts or a subscription.
column7: It does not copy McAfee's browser or identity products; no app can make unsafe clicks harmless.

column5: Linux does not need Avast's always-on antivirus; ClamAV is provided for checking files.
column6: The system uses signed software, updates and permissions instead of a noisy security suite.
column7: This is not a like-for-like Avast bundle; it focuses on safer defaults and scans when wanted.

column5: Linux does not need Defender's always-on antivirus; ClamAV is provided for file scans.
column6: The built-in firewall, signed updates and app permissions do most of the protective work.
column7: The protection model is different, and no antivirus should be treated as a guarantee.

column5: ClamAV can scan suspicious downloads and files instead of Malwarebytes' Windows scanner.
column6: It is open and does not upsell protection, while Linux permissions and updates provide everyday defence.
column7: ClamAV is useful for files, but it is not Malwarebytes' Windows real-time remediation system.

column5: A registry cleaner is not needed on Linux because there is no Windows registry to clean.
column6: Apps and updates come from maintained packages, and the disk-space picture shows real files safely.

column6: The open version covers server uploads and downloads without the paid add-ons.

column6: It keeps the familiar two-pane server layout, so there is little new to learn.

column7: The terminal is different from PuTTY's window; saved sessions and keys must be moved separately.

column6: The included open backup app never requires a cloud account.
column7: This is not hosted Backblaze storage; keep an encrypted off-site copy yourself for fire or theft.

column6: It is the best open choice for a local KeePass vault; Bitwarden is also installed for syncing.
column7: KeePass files work well; browser setup and cloud sync are manual rather than automatic.

column5: Bitwarden replaces 1Password with an encrypted password vault across your devices.
column6: It is open source, independently checked and already installed with a guided setup.
column7: Export and import your vault; item types, families and some business features differ.

column5: Bitwarden replaces LastPass with an open encrypted password vault.
column6: It is already installed and can import a LastPass export after you confirm.
column7: Passwords and notes transfer well; the exact folders and sharing features can differ.

column5: Bitwarden replaces Dashlane with an open encrypted password manager.
column6: It works across devices and is already installed with a beginner setup page.
column7: Export the old vault deliberately; payment details, sharing and special item types may need checking.

column5: OBS Studio is already installed for recording the screen and live streaming.

column7: Your scenes and plugins need exporting or recreation; the recording features are the same.

column5: Blender is already installed for 3D modelling, animation and rendering.
